newsitem.title: INDONESIA: New Thai leader to make courtesy visit to Indonesia.
newsitem.headline: New Thai leader to make courtesy visit to Indonesia.

text.p: Thailand's new Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh arrives in Jakarta on Thursday for what diplomats said would be a courtesy visit to the region's elder statesman, Indonesia's President Suharto.
Diplomats said it was customary for a new leader among the seven-member Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) to first make a round of fellow ASEAN states.
Suharto, in power for 30 years this year, is a co-founder of ASEAN and the longest-serving leader in the region.
The grouping comprises Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, the Philippines, Thailand and Vietnam.
Chavalit, who heads the New Aspiration Party (NAP), took office in November after general elections in Thailand.
He also has personal ties to Indonesia. His wife Phanklua was born here and later immigrated to Thailand.
Chavalit, who is also defence minister, will be accompanied by Foreign Minister Prachuab Chaiyasarn.
His six-party coalition has had a rocky first month in power due mainly to Thailand's sluggish economy, which the prime minister has said would be his top priority.
Thai diplomatic sources said there were no outstanding issues between the two countries.
"They will have open-ended discussions, but there are no particular issues," one source said. The talks would cover bilateral relations and cooperation in various areas.

Officials said Chavalit was due to arrive at Jakarta's Halim Perdanakusuma airbase at midday (0500 GMT) on Thursday. The first day would be mainly ceremonial, with a state banquet hosted by Suharto in the evening.
Talks would be held on Friday morning before the Thai party left.
